newsitem.title: USA: TCI Satellite Entertainment CEO makes push.
newsitem.headline: TCI Satellite Entertainment CEO makes push.

text.p: TCI Satellite Entertainment Inc President and Chief Executive Gary Howard said on Wednesday he wants the recently spun-off company to expand from its rural base and go after suburban and urban satellite-dish markets.

The company, which was to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq, had about 735,000 customers as of September, primarily in rural areas. Howard would not project the size of the market he believes the company can capture, but noted that the market up for grabs is sizeable.

"There are roughly 40 million homes that don't take cable" television, he said during a news conference in midtown Manhattan. "Fifty percent of that universe said they would be very interested and would subscribe to a service" like the company's Prime Star, he said.
Tele-Communications Inc has a 21 percent stake in Prime Star, a partnership that includes Time Warner Inc, Comcast Corp, Cox Communications Inc and General Electric Co.
The push for the urban and suburban market would coincide with the introduction of a smaller dish, which is expected to take place in the Fall of 1997, he said.
The new dish will be about 13.5 inches in diameter and offer about 150 different channels. The current dish is between 36 inches in diameter and offers about 90 channels.
Howard said it is too early to offer a price range for the new dish.
The spinoff of TCI Satellite Entertainment from Tele-Communications Inc was approved in mid-November.
